questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Proxy pattern?

options.text: Provide a surrogate with the same interface that controls access to another object
Add responsibilities to an object dynamically
Share intrinsic state across many objects

questions.explanation: Proxy controls access via a same-interface stand-in. Adding responsibilities = Decorator; converting = Adapter; sharing state = Flyweight.

questions.prompt: Match each proxy variety to what it does.

pairs.right: Defers creating an expensive object until needed
Represents an object in another process/machine
Stores results to avoid repeat work

questions.explanation: Proxies are categorized by purpose: lazy loading, access control, remoting, and caching.

questions.prompt: Both Proxy and Decorator keep the same interface as the wrapped object. What distinguishes them?

options.text: Decorator adds responsibilities; Proxy controls access
Decorator changes the interface; Proxy does not
Proxy adds responsibilities; Decorator controls access

questions.explanation: The tell is intent: Decorator enriches behavior, Proxy gatekeeps access (lazy, secure, cached, remote).

questions.prompt: Match each wrapper pattern to how its interface relates to the wrapped object.

pairs.right: A new, simpler interface over many classes
The same interface, with added behavior

questions.explanation: Adapter converts, Facade simplifies many, Decorator adds behavior (same interface), Proxy controls access (same interface).

questions.prompt: What does a virtual proxy do?

options.text: Defers creating an expensive real object until it is actually needed
Clones the real object on every call

questions.explanation: A virtual proxy provides lazy loading — the costly object is built on first use, or never if unused.

questions.prompt: What is JavaScript's built-in Proxy object?

options.text: A language feature that wraps a target and traps operations like get/set/has
A way to guarantee a single instance

questions.explanation: The built-in Proxy intercepts fundamental operations on a target object — one way to implement proxy-like access control.
